projects.name: Akin
projects.tagline: Keeps students in class when they cannot afford the commute.
projects.problem: In a large cohort, attendance is bimodal. Some students quietly drop out because the daily trip costs more than they have, and the gap stays invisible until someone has already stopped showing up. A public donation board humiliates. Ad-hoc cash never reconciles. Just carpool has no safety net.
projects.solution: Two coordinated rails over one shared identity and an audited ledger: a pooled cash Transport Fund that givers contribute to through Paystack, and an in-kind ride network. The metric it optimises for is retention with dignity, not money raised.
projects.system: A Fiber HTTP and WebSocket API, GORM over Postgres, Redis for sessions and cache, Svix for webhooks, Resend for email, goose migrations, role-aware flows, and a full audit trail. A Vite, React and TypeScript PWA fronts it for low-end and offline-prone campus phones.
projects.dsa: The wallet ledger uses pessimistic row locking (GORM clause.Locking strength UPDATE, a SELECT FOR UPDATE) so two concurrent disbursements can never double-spend the fund. Worker pools coordinate the two rails in real time.
projects.why: Go and Fiber for concurrent coordination of two rails plus live WebSocket updates. A React PWA because the people who need this are on cheap phones and flaky networks, and the app has to load anyway.
projects.innovation: Dignity is encoded into the architecture, not bolted on. A cash rail and an in-kind rail reconcile inside one ledger, so help looks like a quiet transaction rather than a charity feed with someone's name on it.
metrics: designed for a 500-person cohort, scales to a campus
projects.potential: Campus-wide rollouts, NGO and CSR-funded programs, and any community where transport cost is a silent dropout driver.

projects.name: Corvus
projects.problem: nmap, masscan and rustscan answer one question, what is open right now, then throw the state away. In security the signal that matters is the change: what appeared, what vanished, when, and why.
projects.solution: A stateful network intelligence engine. Corvus versions every host, port and service observation as a time series, diffs each scan against history, fuses passive intelligence before scanning, surfaces anomalies, correlates CVEs, and answers questions in plain English. Solo-built full-stack: 10.7k lines of Go across 24 packages plus a 7.6k-line Next.js dashboard.
projects.system: One Go binary exposes a CLI, a Bubble Tea TUI, and a Fiber REST API with WebSocket streaming. Observations persist in an embedded bbolt store. Nodes coordinate over an encrypted UDP gossip mesh. The Next.js 16 frontend renders scans, host history, the mesh, and the natural-language ask view.
projects.dsa: Temporal records are keyed by big-endian timestamps, so the store's natural key order is chronological and history range-scans become a single cursor seek. The diff engine is a set reconciliation of ports seen this scan against ports the store believes open, which is how closed ports get detected. Token-bucket rate limiting governs scan rate, and worker pools fan out the scanning.
projects.why: Go gives a single static binary, goroutine-driven concurrency for scanning thousands of endpoints at once, and a first-class network stack. Next.js carries the streaming dashboard.
projects.innovation: Change is a first-class event, not a diff you compute by hand. Predictive intelligence scores a target from DNS, ASN and certificate-transparency data before a single packet is sent, so scanning starts smart instead of brute-forcing 65,535 ports.
metrics: thousands of hosts scanned concurrently per node
sub-second delta detection per scan cycle
horizontal scaling via a leaderless mesh
projects.potential: Continuous attack-surface monitoring and cloud-drift detection as a product. The temporal core is a moat competitors structurally lack.

projects.name: go-payroll-engine
projects.tagline: Async bulk salary disbursement, built to fintech production standards.
projects.problem: Paying thousands of people at once is a correctness problem, not a CRUD problem. Duplicate payouts, failed retries and compliance are where payroll systems break. And the salary-advance market beside it traps workers in roughly 30 percent interest loans.
projects.solution: An async bulk disbursement engine that batches payouts onto a job queue, dedups aggressively, and treats every payment as idempotent. Compliance with PCI DSS, NDPR, SOC 2 and CBN is designed in from the start rather than retrofitted.
projects.system: A Gin API in front of GORM, Postgres and Redis, with asynq running the disbursement workers off a queue, Prometheus for observability, golang-migrate for schema, and JWT auth. Provider webhooks feed back through deduplicated handlers.
projects.dsa: A Redis-backed Bloom filter gives O(1) duplicate-webhook detection at roughly 1 percent false-positive and zero false-negative. An LRU cache holds per-key rate limiters so each tenant is throttled independently. Idempotency keys in Redis with a 24h TTL make retries safe. asynq provides priority worker queues.
projects.why: Go for high-throughput concurrent disbursement with predictable latency, a mature async-queue ecosystem in asynq, and a strong fintech tooling story.
projects.innovation: Earned-wage access without the debt trap. Instead of a 30 percent loan, an employee draws a slice of pay they have already earned, accrued daily from verified work. Three guardrails keep it healthy: a tapering access curve that shrinks the available percentage as payday nears, an automatic micro-savings skim that locks a small cut of every advance into savings, and a financial-health score that rewards restraint with better terms. Early access that builds a cushion instead of a habit, riding the same idempotent, deduped rails the engine already runs.
metrics: thousands of payees per batch run
near-zero duplicate payouts via bloom and idempotency
bounded p99 via async queue back-pressure
projects.potential: Payroll-as-infrastructure for African SMEs, with the earned-wage-access layer as a humane alternative to predatory advances.
projects.note: Work in progress. Earned-wage-access layer in design.

projects.name: Bukr
projects.tagline: Cloud-native ticketing where inventory cannot oversell.
projects.problem: Event ticketing fails in two predictable ways. It oversells under burst load when everyone buys at once, and the fee model quietly erodes trust. Both are architecture problems, not bad luck.
projects.solution: A polyglot modular monolith. A Go and Fiber gateway owns auth, events, users and orchestration. A Rust and Axum core owns the correctness and throughput critical path: tickets, the gate scanner, payments and analytics. Supabase and Postgres for data and auth, Redis for cache and sessions.
projects.system: Gateway and core talk over gRPC and HTTP and split by responsibility rather than fashion. Redis caches hot reads and holds sessions. Payment integration, an influencer and affiliate portal, credits, and a QR gate scanner round out the surface. A Vite and React SPA fronts it.
projects.dsa: SELECT FOR UPDATE row locking inside transactions guards invite-token redemption, credit balances and influencer earnings, so two concurrent requests cannot double-redeem or oversell. The system uses heap-based ordering and per-route rate limiting, and the gateway-core split is itself a decision about where correctness must be strongest.
projects.why: Go for the I/O-bound gateway where developer velocity and concurrency win, and Rust for the hot path where memory safety and raw throughput on ticket inventory and payments matter most.
projects.innovation: A dual-language modular monolith that puts the language where it earns its keep, plus an influencer-driven distribution engine and a hybrid smart-pricing fee model designed against local market benchmarks.
metrics: oversell-proof sales under burst via row locks
low-latency gate validation from the Rust core
11k Go plus a Rust core plus a 175-file React frontend
projects.potential: A pan-African ticketing and event platform where reliability under a flash sale is the whole differentiator.

projects.name: Fleetform
projects.tagline: Infrastructure as code with a memory-safe core and a live graph.
projects.problem: IaC planners are powerful but opaque. You apply and hope the ordering is right. And the dominant engines run on a garbage-collected runtime where a state-graph bug becomes a footgun.
projects.solution: A Rust core engine that plans and applies infrastructure with a memory-safe state and dependency model, paired with a Go and Fiber web dashboard that streams plan progress and renders the dependency graph in real time. HCL config, a module system, and multi-backend state across file, S3 and Consul.
projects.system: The Rust core owns parsing, the resource graph and apply. The Go and Fiber layer serves the dashboard and pushes live updates over WebSocket. Proto definitions bridge the two.
projects.dsa: The heart of the planner is a resource dependency DAG with topological sort via petgraph toposort and cycle detection, so apply order is provably correct and cycles fail loudly instead of corrupting state.
projects.why: Rust for the safety-critical graph and state engine where a bug means broken infrastructure, and Go with Fiber for the real-time web layer where iteration speed matters.
projects.innovation: A live dependency-graph dashboard over a compiled, memory-safe core. An IaC tool that shows you the shape of your infrastructure as it plans.
metrics: multi-backend state across file, S3 and Consul
projects.potential: An open-source IaC alternative for teams that want safety and visibility, not just parity.
projects.note: Early-stage. Rust core plus Go UI.

projects.name: OpsTool
projects.tagline: DevOps automation: Go performance, Python reach.
projects.problem: Ops automation usually ends up as a pile of unscheduled scripts with no visibility. Teams need scheduled, observable, repeatable automation behind one surface.
projects.solution: A platform that pairs a Go API for the performant concurrent core with Python workers for the automation ecosystem, scheduled and observable, with a dashboard on top.
projects.system: A Gin API over GORM, Postgres and Redis, gorilla/websocket for live job status, Prometheus metrics, and robfig/cron driving scheduled jobs. Python handles the automation glue, and a frontend dashboard surfaces it.
projects.dsa: Cron-based scheduling for recurring jobs, mutex-guarded shared state for concurrent workers, and per-route rate limiting. The Go and Python split is the core system-design call: performance where it counts, ecosystem where it helps.
projects.why: Go for the concurrent, low-latency API and scheduler, and Python because the operational automation libraries and glue live there.
projects.innovation: A hybrid internal-developer-platform shape: one language for speed, one for breadth, unified behind a single scheduled and observable control plane.
projects.potential: An internal developer platform for small teams that cannot justify a full platform org.

projects.name: CarbonAPI
projects.tagline: Instant carbon footprint calculation as an API.
projects.problem: Every company now has to track emissions for ESG compliance, but the incumbents are slow, taking days to weeks, expensive at 10K to 100K dollar licenses, and manual through spreadsheet uploads. Carbon math should not take a procurement cycle.
projects.solution: A Go REST API that returns a carbon footprint for any activity in milliseconds, deployed reproducibly through Terraform. Post an activity, get a number.
projects.system: A stateless Go service over emission-factor lookup tables, containerised and provisioned with Terraform so it scales horizontally behind a load balancer. No session state means trivial replication.
projects.dsa: Emission-factor lookup tables for O(1) factor resolution, and a stateless compute model so throughput scales linearly with instances.
projects.why: Go for fast cold-start, a single cheap binary, and predictable latency at API scale, the qualities that let a calculation API undercut enterprise licences.
projects.innovation: Carbon as an API. A primitive you embed in a checkout, a logistics quote or a sustainability dashboard, rather than a six-figure platform.
projects.potential: Embed in e-commerce checkouts and logistics pricing, a usage-priced ESG primitive for developers.

projects.name: ERA Full Cloud DevOps
projects.tagline: Taking an app cloud-native, end to end.
projects.problem: Plenty of apps work on a laptop and fall over in production. The gap is operational: reproducible infrastructure, orchestration, autoscaling, event flow and security.
projects.solution: An Enterprise Resource Allocation app transformed into a cloud-native platform: complete AWS infrastructure as code, Kubernetes orchestration with autoscaling, event-driven messaging with Kafka, and container-security best practices.
projects.system: Terraform provisions AWS. Kubernetes runs the services with horizontal autoscaling. Kafka carries events between microservices. CI/CD automates build and deploy. The application is the payload, the cloud architecture is the point.
projects.dsa: Event-driven decoupling via Kafka topics and capacity-aware scheduling through Kubernetes autoscaling policies. System design over algorithms here.
projects.why: This one is infrastructure-first. It exists to demonstrate the CKA and AWS skill set: making something real run reproducibly and scale on demand.
projects.innovation: A legacy-to-cloud-native transformation captured as code, with architecture decision records, so the how is reproducible rather than folklore.
projects.potential: A template for taking ordinary applications to production-grade cloud infrastructure.
projects.note: Application is Node. The value is the cloud and infrastructure layer.

projects.name: ProductCatalogAPI
projects.tagline: An e-commerce API that refuses to oversell.
projects.problem: During traffic spikes, multiple customers buy the last unit at the same instant, and naive systems oversell, creating refunds, angry customers and reconciliation pain.
projects.solution: A clean-architecture .NET Core Web API for catalog and orders, with concurrency control that makes simultaneous purchases safe and stock decrements correct.
projects.system: ASP.NET Core with Entity Framework Core over Postgres, SQLite in dev, organised in SOLID layers. Order placement runs inside transactions with concurrency checks on stock.
projects.dsa: Concurrency control on inventory through row and optimistic locking and transactional order processing, so the last-unit race resolves to exactly one winner.
projects.why: .NET and EF Core for a strongly-typed, clean-architecture e-commerce backend. Included to show range beyond Go: the concurrency thinking is the same, the runtime is different.
projects.innovation: A reference implementation of correctness under concurrency for inventory, the failure mode most e-commerce demos ignore.
projects.potential: A correctness baseline any commerce backend can adopt for inventory integrity.
